claims.text: Large language models integrated with retrieval-augmented generation may still produce unsupported or contradictory claims relative to retrieved content.

Finetuning a relatively small LLM on the RAGTruth dataset achieves a competitive level of performance in hallucination detection compared to prompt-based approaches using state-of-the-art models like GPT-4.

evidence.description: Despite the integration of RAG, LLMs may still present unsupported or contradictory claims to the retrieved contents.

we show that using a high-quality dataset such as RAGTruth, it is possible to finetune a relatively small LLM and achieve a competitive level of performance in hallucination detection when compared to the existing prompt-based approaches using state-of-the-art large language models such as GPT-4.

methodologies.name: RAGTruth Corpus Construction and Annotation
methodologies.description: A hallucination corpus comprising nearly 18,000 naturally generated LLM responses under standard RAG frameworks with manual case- and word-level annotations.

limitations.text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models still present unsupported or contradictory claims despite using retrieved content.
